core.title: Bind each test's acceptance/DESIRED_OUTCOME binding to a URN the plan declares
core.given: The repository's plan declares acceptances and a test file of any test role — unit, acceptance or end-to-end — carries an acceptance or DESIRED OUTCOME binding (the binding syntax comes from the profile)
core.when: the binding is checked (test or binding changed, plan changed, or any CI run)
core.then: Every acceptance and DESIRED OUTCOME URN named in a test's binding MUST be stated somewhere under the plan root.
prefer: Repair the binding from the plan, not the plan from the test: the plan is authoritative during test authoring.
Stale binding or renamed acceptance: point the test at the declared acceptance it actually exercises and proves (the binding syntax and URN shapes come from the profile).
Test proves different behavior: bind it to that behavior's existing declared acceptance; if it does not prove the claimed acceptance, adjust the test, not the label.
No declared acceptance fits: return to the authorized planning flow so the behavior is declared deliberately before the test claims coverage.
avoid: Creating, renaming or repurposing a plan acceptance, or inventing one, merely to make a test resolve or clear this finding; plan additions are planner work justified by the behavior.
Binding to a convenient but semantically unrelated declared acceptance (the dangerous gaming case).
unless: The plan declares no acceptances at all: NOT_APPLICABLE.
The test has no binding at all: owned by the companion rule that requires a binding to be present (no double-count).
core.why: A binding to an acceptance that exists nowhere attributes the test to nothing, making coverage figures fiction: a NAME accepted where a CLAIM is required.
evidence: The check collects every acceptance and DESIRED OUTCOME URN token stated under the plan root and reports zero test bindings naming a URN absent from that set.

Reviewer confirms each binding's acceptance is the one the test case genuinely exercises and asserts (resolution is only the structural half of truth; a resolving binding is still semantically false if the case exercises or asserts something else).
Diff shows no plan acceptance created, renamed or repurposed solely to make an existing test resolve.
verification: Repository-level structural check, not an edited-file selector: it examines every existing test binding across all test roles — unit, acceptance and end-to-end tests alike, whether or not touched by the current change — and is re-triggered when either side of a binding changes (binding added or edited, plan acceptance renamed or removed) and on every CI run. The profile's role assignment supplies the exhaustive mapping of the stack's test files onto the test roles.

Resolution procedure: recursively collect every acceptance and DESIRED OUTCOME URN stated anywhere under the plan root (every artifact in that tree, at any depth), then flag any test whose binding names a URN the plan never mentions. The plan root, the binding syntax and the URN shapes are profile data.

Declared URNs are read as TOKENS rather than parsed structurally, on purpose: acceptances are stated under several keys across the plan's documents, and a binding resolves if the plan states that URN anywhere. Over-accepting is the safe direction — the failure caught is a reference to something the plan never mentions.

Return NOT_APPLICABLE when the repository declares no acceptances at all: a repository with no plan has nothing to resolve against, and reporting there would fire on every unplanned project rather than on a broken reference.
Do not report tests with no binding at all: the companion rule that requires a binding to be present owns that case; reporting both would double-count one defect.
The repository-level precondition (the plan declares at least one acceptance) is evaluated by this repository-level check, not by a task-level fact.

What the check does not cover: semantic truth. Resolution is only the structural half — a binding can resolve and still be semantically false if the case exercises or asserts something else; that judgment stays with review and is a candidate separate obligation.
Term resolvable_binding: a binding whose URN is stated somewhere in the repository's plan, so the test is attributable to a declared obligation rather than to a name.
Diagnostic hint: a renamed acceptance is the common mechanical cause; a convenient but semantically unrelated acceptance is the dangerous gaming case.
Disposition strict, severity 4: a finding is not suppressible and fails CI.
Division of labor: the neutral core owns the shape of acceptance/DESIRED_OUTCOME plan artifacts; only a stack realization can see whether that stack's tests resolve into them.

fires: A test's acceptance binding names a URN that appears nowhere in the plan artifacts.
A test's DESIRED OUTCOME binding names a DESIRED OUTCOME that the plan never mentions.
A plan-only change renames an acceptance and existing, untouched test bindings still carry the old URN.
doesNotFire: A test carrying no binding at all (owned by the companion rule that requires a binding to be present).
A repository whose plan declares no acceptances at all (NOT_APPLICABLE).
A binding whose URN is stated anywhere in the plan, under any key in any plan document.

profileRequirements.meaning: Exhaustive mapping of the checked test population onto the test roles: the stack's test files (unit, acceptance and end-to-end alike) are all in scope, and the check examines every existing test file carrying an acceptance or DESIRED OUTCOME binding, whether or not it is touched by the current change; this is also how test-language scoping is expressed (the stack's own test files), rather than through a language key.
profileRequirements.bunValue: Bun stack realization; only Bun test files are checked. Any existing Bun test file carrying a `// Acceptance:` or `// DESIRED_OUTCOME:` header, whether or not it is touched by the current change.

profileRequirements.meaning: Root of plan artifacts: declared acceptance/DESIRED_OUTCOME URNs are collected recursively under this root, and every test binding must resolve against it.
The syntax by which a test file binds itself to an acceptance artifact (header comment, decorator or annotation in the stack).
The syntax by which a test file binds itself to a DESIRED OUTCOME artifact.
URN shape of an acceptance; recognized as a resolving token wherever the plan states it.
URN shape of a DESIRED OUTCOME artifact.

neutralityNotes: The obligation is fully neutral: every bound acceptance/DESIRED_OUTCOME URN must be stated somewhere under the plan root. All concrete syntax (binding headers, URN shapes, plan root, test-population assignment) moves to profileRequirements, so the core plus the Bun profile plus the bunOnly items imposes exactly the bun.json obligation. Population scope: the Bun text checks 'any existing Bun test file', so the core's file_kind fact lists the complete set of test roles in the vocabulary — unit_test, acceptance_test AND e2e_test — and the profile's roles.assignment carries the exhaustive mapping (only the stack's own test files; every existing one carrying a binding, touched or not), leaving nothing to a future profile. bun.json establishes no test-file naming convention, so no suffix.* keys are claimed; test-language scoping is likewise expressed through role assignment, not through the production-language key. roots.plan holds the root path 'plan'; the 'plan/**' recursion is expressed as recursive collection under that root in core:verification. Residual choices: sibling-rule references are generic in the core ('the companion rule that requires a binding to be present') because rule ids are realization-specific; detector family/finding ids and the verbatim fix-hint snippet remain Bun-only, with bun.json serving as the worked reference example; the strict severity-4 disposition is stated once in core verification, not duplicated per field.
